text:
nina: hi team, day 1 here. downloaded kubeconfig from the portal and appended it to my ~/.kube/config. now `kubectl config get-contexts` shows two entries both named `redwood-dev` and i'm not sure which one points at prod. i want to avoid any chances of touching prod. any safe checks?

josh: welcome! quick checks: `kubectl config current-context` and then `kubectl config view --raw -o jsonpath='{.clusters[?(@.name=="'$(kubectl config current-context)'")].cluster.server}'` will show the api server URL. if it has `prod` in hostname, don't run writes.

nina: ran that and one has `api.k8s.redwood.prod.internal` so yikes. i never ran a write but i did `kubectl get ns` earlier and it errored with Forbidden so i think reads are limited anyway.

devex-bot: Onboarding note: safe kubeconfig workflows are at https://docs.internal/redwood/onboarding/k8s#safe-kubeconfig. Tip: keep per-cluster files under `~/.kube/contexts/` and use `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml:$KUBECONFIG` instead of merging.

josh: since names collided, rename the portal context on a copy so you won't accidentally switch. Example: `cp portal.yaml ~/.kube/contexts/dev-portal.yaml && kubectl config rename-context redwood-dev redwood-dev-portal --kubeconfig=~/.kube/contexts/dev-portal.yaml`

nina: i'm not comfortable editing creds locally. can infra-triage help create a safe per-user context or give me a temp namespace binding so i can test without touching anything global?

infra-triage: @nina yes we can. paste the output of `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.users[0].name}'` (only the exact user string we need). Also confirm your portal ticket id if you opened one.

nina: output: nina@redwood. ticket ONB-611 (created earlier).

infra-triage: creating namespace-scoped RoleBinding `onboard-nina-view` in `team-nina` binding `view` to user `nina@redwood`, expiry 72h. will attach ONB-611.

sre-ops: done. you should have `view` in `team-nina`. test with `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-nina` then `kubectl get pods -n team-nina`.

nina: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-nina` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n team-nina` shows two pods. thanks!

josh: small extra tips: 1) install `kubectx` & `kubens` 2) keep a backup of your original `~/.kube/config` as `~/.kube/config.bak` before editing 3) use `yq` to rewrite context/user names in copies, eg `yq eval '.contexts[].name |= . + "-portal"' portal.yaml > ~/.kube/contexts/dev-portal.yaml`

nina: would it be possible to get a reminder before the temporary RoleBinding expires? i don't want to get locked out mid-debug.

infra-triage: yes, onboarding-bot will post a 24h reminder. if you need more time, reopen ONB-611 and request extension with PR link or reason. if it's ongoing work we'll move you to a team role instead of temp access.

devex-bot: Also note: for automation use cases we prefer service accounts. If you ever need a token for CI, open a request with the repo name and we can provision a namespaced SA with short-lived tokens.

nina: perfect. one last safety Q: is there any hook to prevent accidental `kubectl delete` in prod from junior shells?

sre-ops: we enforce guardrails: prod requires an additional approval step for destructive kubectl commands via a short-lived privilege escalation and we have audit alerts. still, avoid running destructive commands until you're comfortable. use `--dry-run=client` where possible and check `kubectl auth can-i delete pods -n <ns>` first.

nina: thanks everyone, saved me from a potential mess. closing the thread :pray:
